---
title: "Multi-site pipelines and caching"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(normet)

covariates <- c("ws", "wd", "temp", "RH", "atmos_pres", "blh", "tcc", "tp", "ssrd")
predictors <- c(covariates, "date_unix", "day_julian", "weekday", "hour")
```

## Multi-site pipelines

A station network is one long table with a site column (`df_network` below,
with a `site` column). The multi-site drivers split it by site, run the same
analysis on each site in its own worker process, and bind the results back
together with the site column appended.

```{r}
# Normalise all sites in parallel
multi <- nm_do_all_multisite(
  df            = df_network,
  site_col      = "site",
  target        = "NO2",
  covariates    = predictors,
  resample_vars = covariates,
  n_samples     = 300
)
# return_models = TRUE also returns each site's model: list(res = , models = )

# Decompose every site
multi_emi <- nm_decompose_multisite(
  df = df_network, site_col = "site", method = "emission",
  target = "NO2", covariates = predictors
)
```

`nm_multisite_apply()` runs any function of the form `function(df, ...)` once
per site:

```{r}
site_summary <- function(df, ...) {
  data.frame(n = nrow(df), mean_no2 = mean(df$NO2, na.rm = TRUE))
}
nm_multisite_apply(df_network, site_col = "site", func = site_summary, n_cores = 4)
```

`site_kwarg =` names an argument of `func` that receives the site's value, for
functions that need to know which site they are working on. Pass `n_cores` to
limit the number of worker processes.

## Caching

`nm_do_all()`, `nm_build_model()`, `nm_train_model()`, `nm_normalise()` and
`nm_decompose()` accept a `cache_dir`. Their results are keyed by a SHA-1 hash
of the data and the configuration, so a second run with unchanged inputs is
read from disk instead of recomputed:

```{r}
results <- nm_do_all(
  df = my1, target = "NO2", covariates = predictors, resample_vars = covariates,
  cache_dir = ".normet_cache"
)
# The same call again returns at once, from .normet_cache/<key>.rds
```

The hashing helpers are exported, so your own slow steps can be cached the
same way:

```{r}
cache <- nm_make_cache(".normet_cache")          # creates the directory
key   <- nm_config_hash(nm_dataframe_hash(my1), target = "NO2", n_samples = 300)
path  <- file.path(cache$path, paste0(key, ".rds"))

if (file.exists(path)) {
  result <- readRDS(path)
} else {
  result <- my_slow_function(my1)
  saveRDS(result, path)
}
```

`nm_model_hash()` hashes a trained model. When the memoise package is
installed, `cache$memoise` is `memoise::memoise`, for function-level
memoisation.
